To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the HN(C)(N) experiment is an efficient method for rapid assignment of (15N,13C) labeled peptides and proteins, and that the HN-C(alpha) J couplings estimated from this experiment correlate well with the backbone torsion angles.

the HN(C)(N) experiment provides a rapid method for sequential assignment of backbone atoms in proteins and that the intensities of peaks in the F2-F3 planes provide estimates of 1J(Calpha-N) couplings that are useful for structural studies.
the HN(C)(N) experiment provides an enhancement in the speed and reliability of resonance assignment and also provides quantitative information on psi torsion angles in medium size proteins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of a new experiment for protein NMR structure determination.
the development of new experiments for the study of protein structure and function.
the development of new methods for rapid resonance assignment and structural characterization of proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HN(C) N is the best experiment for rapid and accurate resonance assignment in medium sized proteins.

the HN(CN) experiment is a very useful and powerful method for the rapid assignment of backbone amide resonances and for the rapid estimation of the one-bond N-C(alpha) coupling constants, which correlate well with psi torsion angle in medium-sized proteins.

the method provides a rapid estimation of 13C(alpha)-15N J-couplings, with an estimated error of approximately 10% and that these couplings are correlated to psi torsion angles with a standard deviation of approximately 15 degrees.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HN(C)-N experiment is a useful tool for structural genomics.
HN(C) N is a powerful experiment for protein structure determination and the present approach for estimation of coupling constants would be useful for structural genomics.
HN(C)NH and HN(C)C are two complementary experiments that together can provide a complete assignment of the backbone and sidechain resonances in proteins in a single experiment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HN(C) NMR experiment is a valuable addition to the arsenal of NMR experiments that can be used in structural genomics.
the HN(C)(N) experiment is a useful experiment for rapid structural genomics.
the J(N-Calpha) values are very useful in the determination of psi torsion angles and the approach presented here is very fast and easy to implement.
